page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running on an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The CPU hardware includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a 105 MB L3 cache, with support for instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES. The instance provides 672.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high density of 28.0 GB per vCPU. No local ephemeral storage is included in this instance configuration.

Performance benchmarking shows strong memory subsystem results, including a top-quartile PassMark memory score and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec. Compute testing across stress-ng, GeekBench, and PassMark CPU suites yields benchmark scores in the average range. Multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput also align with average platform performance. The primary design tradeoff of the instance is its constrained CPU core count relative to its large RAM allocation, prioritizing memory capacity over massive parallel execution.

From a cost efficiency perspective, this configuration allows organizations running software licensed on a per-core basis to access substantial memory resources without paying for unneeded vCPUs. This makes the instance suitable for enterprise resource planning platforms such as SAP HANA, large relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
